question.value: How do the formation and early evolution of Super Star Clusters (SSCs) in NGC 4945 proceed, and to what extent does positive feedback from the molecular outflow trigger sequential SSC formation versus quenching?

evidence.quote: Then the study of the formation and early evolution of the SSCs in NGC 4945, when compared to the one already carried out toward NGC 253 ((cite: Rico20; Rico21; Rico22)), has the potential to provide further information on the evolution of the starburst and to establish to what extent the sequential star formation (positive feedback) also dominates at later stages or whether the SSC formation has been quenched.
In this work we use ALMA data to study the early evolutionary stage of the proto-SSCs using the HCN and HC$_3$N vibrationally excited emission in NGC 4945.
We obtained the HCN, HC$_3$N and CS images toward NGC 4945 from the ALMA Science Archive data (Project-IDs: 2016.1.01135.S and 2018.1.01236.S).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.01135.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01236.S.

analysis_steps.goal: Select sample of 14 Super Star Clusters (SSCs) across evolutionary stages

method.value: Select 14 SSCs out of 27 in Emig et al. (2020) by peak emission of vibrationally excited HC3N,v71 or HCN*, and by dust continuum peak at ~350 GHz with only CS and ground-state HC3N emissions and high stellar mass (10^5.1 - 10^5.7 M_sun)

evidence.quote: We selected 14 SSCs, out of 27 found by (cite: Emig20), in two ways: i) by the peak emissions of the vibrationally excited HC$_3$N,v$_{71}$ or the HCN$^*$ and, ii) by the dust continuum peak at $\sim$350 GHz with only CS emissions.

In the latter case, we searched for the SSCs characterized by high stellar mass (10$^{5.1}$-10$^{5.7}$ $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$) as measured by the radio continuum emission together with high ($>$10$^{5.0}$ $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$) or low ($<$10$^{5.0}$ $M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$) gas mass ((cite: Emig20)).

key_parameters.value: Stellar mass range 10^5.1 - 10^5.7 M_sun; gas mass threshold 10^5.0 M_sun

analysis_steps.goal: Identify molecular lines and fit LTE line profiles to derive rotational and vibrational temperatures (T_rot and T_vib)

method.value: Simulate line profiles under LTE conditions including opacity effects for a given source size using MADCUBA SLIM; derive T_vib from transitions with the same J across different vibrational states, and T_rot from rotational transitions within the same vibrational state (or from CS and HC3N,v0)

evidence.quote: We used the MADCUBA’s tool SLIM (Spectral Line Identification and Modelling; (cite: Martin19)) to identify the molecular lines and to perform the Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) analysis.

We derive the excitation temperature of the vibrationally excited levels (hereafter, $T_{\rm vib}$) by only considered transitions with the same J but arising from different vibrationally excited states.

To derive the excitation temperature of the rotational levels within the vibrational states (hereafter, $T_{\rm rot}$) we combined all the rotational transitions arising from the same vibrationally states (ground state, $v_{\rm 71}$, $v_{\rm 61}$ and $v_{\rm 72}$).
Throughout the paper, we adopted a systemic velocity of 550 km s$^{-1}$, based on CO observations ((cite: Dahlem93)).

assumptions.value: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE); T_vib ~ T_dust because HC3N* is mid-IR pumped and mid-IR dust emission is optically thick

evidence.quote: SLIM simulates the line profiles under LTE conditions, including opacity effects for a given source size.

Since HC$_3$N$^*$ transitions are excited through the absorption of mid-IR photons and, at these wavelengths the dust emission is optically thick, the vibrational temperature is expected to closely reflect the dust temperature ($T_{\rm vib}$$\sim$$T_{\rm dust}$).

fitting.value: Non-linear least-squares fit using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm in SLIM AUTOFIT

evidence.quote: The AUTOFIT tool in SLIM performs a non-linear least squared fit of the LTE line profiles to the data using Levenberg-Marquartd algorithm.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive apparent and greenhouse-corrected protostellar luminosities (L_p*), protostellar masses (M_p*), and SSC evolutionary ages (t_age)

method.value: Compute apparent luminosity via Stefan-Boltzmann law L_app = 4 * pi * r^2 * sigma * T_vib^4; apply greenhouse correction factor 4/psi ~ 1/10 to get L_p* = (4/psi) * L_app; estimate ages from L_p*/L_ZAMS using t_age = 10^5 / (1 + L_p*/L_ZAMS) yr

evidence.quote: We estimated the apparent luminosity of the proto-SSCs, $L_{\rm app}$, from the $T_{\rm vib}$ ($\sim$$T_{\rm dust}$; Table [2](#Input_data)) and the lower (upper) sizes (Table [3](#Params_physical)) using the Stefan-Boltzmann law: $L_{\rm app}$= 4$\pi$$r^2$ $\sigma$ $T_{\rm vib}^4$.

Our apparent luminosity can be corrected of the green-house effect applying the correction factor 4/$\psi$ to estimate the actual luminosity of proto-stars ($L_{\rm p*}$) as $L_{\rm p*}$ = 4/$\psi$ $\times$ $L_{\rm app}$.

Column (7): Estimated age of SSCs: for $L_{\rm p*}$/$L_{\rm ZAMS}$$\gtrsim$0.05, $t_{\rm age}$=10$^5$/(1 + $L_{\rm p*}$/$L_{\rm ZAMS}$) while for $L_{\rm p*}$/$L_{\rm ZAMS}$$<$0.05, $t_{\rm age}$$\gtrsim$10$^5$ yr (assuming the timescale of an HII region to be $\sim$10$^5$ yr).

claims.hypothesis: Vibrationally excited HCN* emission can trace the proto-SSC phase to later evolutionary stages than HC3N* emission alone.
claims.experiment: Identified HCN(4-3) v2=1 and HC3N v7=1, v6=1, v7=2 emission across 14 SSCs in NGC 4945 and derived their protostellar-to-ZAMS luminosity ratios and ages.
claims.result: 8 SSCs show HCN* emission, 5 of which also have HC3N* (ages 4.9-9.6 x 10^4 yr), while 3 have only HCN* with L_p*/L_ZAMS down to <0.03 and ages >9.4-9.7 x 10^4 yr (close to 10^5 yr).
claims.finding: HCN* emission traces the latest stages of the proto-SSC phase right before reaching the ZAMS stage, after HII regions begin photodissociating more fragile molecules like HC3N.

evidence.loc: HCN* emission. Tracing the latest stages of the proto-SSC phase before reaching the ZAMS-SSC stage.
evidence.quote: Our data also suggest that the proto-HCN are still in the proto-SSC phase since they show HCN$^*$ emission, typical of the SSC phase, without HC$_3$N$^*$ emission counterpart.

evidence.loc: HCN* emission. Tracing the latest stages of the proto-SSC phase before reaching the ZAMS-SSC stage.
evidence.quote: The detection of proto-SSC through HCN allows to trace the proto-SSCs phase to much later stages than in NGC 253 as traced only by HC$_3$N$^*$ emission.

claims.hypothesis: The excitation of the parental molecular cloud is linked to the evolutionary stage of the embedded SSC.
claims.experiment: Derived rotational temperatures T_rot(v0) from ground-state HC3N and CS lines via LTE fitting in MADCUBA SLIM and correlated them with derived SSC ages.
claims.result: A linear trend (rho ~ 0.7) is found between T_rot(v0) and SSC evolutionary stage: proto-HC3N have high T_rot (~65 K), proto-HCN have moderate T_rot (~45 K), and ZAMS-SSCs have low T_rot (~25 K).
claims.finding: Parental cloud excitation declines as the SSC evolves from the embedded protostellar phase to the ZAMS phase, showing that heating by ultracompact HII regions in the ZAMS stage is restricted to their immediate neighborhood while inner warm gas is dissociated.

evidence.quote: The low excitation temperature of the parent cloud when the SSC reaches the ZAMS stage indicates that the heating by its ultracompact HII regions is mainly restricted to their very close neighborhood.

claims.hypothesis: The formation of the youngest proto-SSCs in NGC 4945 was triggered by positive feedback from the molecular outflow.
claims.experiment: Compared the spatial distribution and derived ages of the proto-SSCs with the morphology and dynamical timescale of the CO molecular outflow from Bolatto et al. (2021).
claims.result: The youngest proto-SSCs (proto-HC3N, ages ~7 x 10^4 yr) are located at deprojected distances of ~65 and ~80 pc, bordering the outer edges of the blue- and redshifted CO outflow lobes whose dynamical age (~0.3 Myr) exceeds the proto-SSC ages.
claims.finding: The expansion of the molecular outflow triggered the formation of the youngest generation of proto-SSCs via positive feedback in shocked gas at the outflow edges.

evidence.loc: Triggering the SSC formation. Positive feedback
evidence.quote: From the projected location of basically all the young proto-HC$_3$N, just at the edges of the blue and redshifted lobes of the molecular outflow, we propose that their formation could have been triggered in the shocked gas produced by the expansion of the molecular outflow.

evidence.loc: Triggering the SSC formation. Positive feedback
evidence.quote: Both dynamical times are larger than the age of the proto-SSCs, making it possible the triggering of the most recent episode of massive star formation in NGC 4945 as seen in HC$_3$N$^*$ and HCN$^*$ by the outflow.

claims.hypothesis: Sequential SSC formation explains the differences in SSC ages, gas reservoirs, and spatial distributions between NGC 4945 and the younger starburst NGC 253.
claims.experiment: Compared proto-SSC ages, mean gas mass reservoirs, and radial age gradients in NGC 4945 with those previously measured in NGC 253 by Rico-Villas et al. (2020).
claims.result: Proto-SSCs in NGC 4945 are older (>0.8 x 10^5 yr vs 0.2-0.8 x 10^5 yr in NGC 253), have less than half the mean gas mass reservoir (7.5 x 10^4 M_sun vs ~1.7 x 10^5 M_sun), and have the youngest proto-SSCs closer to the center around the outflow rather than in the outer parts.
claims.finding: The starburst in NGC 4945 (~5 Myr) is in a more evolved stage of sequential SSC formation approaching quenching compared to NGC 253 (~1 Myr), with triggering shifting from central SN-driven overpressure in NGC 253 to molecular outflow shocks in NGC 4945.

evidence.loc: The evolution of the star formation in NGC 4945 and NGC 253. Sequential SSC formation.
evidence.quote: While the typical age of the proto-SSCs in NGC 4945 are about $>$0.8$\times$10$^5$ ($\pm<$0.2$\times$10$^5$) yr, those in NGC 253 are younger, with $t_{\rm age}$$\sim$0.2-0.8 $\times$10$^5$ yr.
SSCs in NGC 4945 are found to be in a more evolved stage than those in NGC 253, consistent with the sequential SSC formation scenario.

why_this_data.value: Vibrationally excited HC3N* and HCN* lines are excited by mid-IR photons and trace the deeply embedded Super Hot Core (proto-SSC) phase that cannot be observed even at mid-IR wavelengths.

evidence.quote: However, the earliest phases of SSCs formation take place deeply embedded in the parental cloud, preventing their observation even at mid-IR.
In this work we use ALMA data to study the early evolutionary stage of the proto-SSCs using the HCN and HC$_3$N vibrationally excited emission in NGC 4945.

why_this_method.value: Following the LTE analysis and luminosity-ratio age-dating method of Rico-Villas et al. (2020) allows direct comparison of proto-SSC physical properties and ages between NGC 4945 and NGC 253.

evidence.quote: Then the study of the formation and early evolution of the SSCs in NGC 4945, when compared to the one already carried out toward NGC 253 ((cite: Rico20; Rico21; Rico22)), has the potential to provide further information on the evolution of the starburst

Following the procedure depicted by (cite: Rico20), we first focus on the determination of the physical parameters (e.g., excitation temperature, column density, radial velocity, line width and source size) of the proto-HC$_3$N in the SHC phase.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Bar-driven gas inflow triggering star formation: rejected because inflow operates from 300 pc down to ~100 pc, whereas the selected SSCs lie at <100 pc well inside the region disturbed by the outflow.

evidence.loc: Triggering the SSC formation. Positive feedback
evidence.quote: (cite: Henkel18) proposed the presence of an inflow of gas in NGC 4945 through a bar from (deprojected) galactocentric radii of 300 pc to $\sim$100 pc toward the nuclear disk, while the central parts ($\lesssim$100 pc) are disturbed by the outflowing gas. Our SSCs fall well within the outflow region, which makes less feasible that the inflow could induce star-formation.

limitations_admitted.value: For proto-HCN and ZAMS-SSCs where HC3N* is not detected, only upper limits on T_vib, source size, and L_p* (and lower limits on age) can be derived.

evidence.quote: For the proto-HCN, only traced by the HCN$^*$ lines, we can only derive an upper limit to $T_{\rm vib}$ ($\sim$$T_{\rm dust}$) from the LTE analysis of HC$_3$N J=11-10 (i.e., 100 GHz; see Table [2](#Input_data)).

When HC$_3$N$^*$ was not detected (i.e., proto-HCN and ZAMS-SSCs), we derived an upper limit to the size using the line intensity of the HC$_3$N,v$_0$, assuming the $T_{\rm vib}$ ($\sim$$T_{\rm dust}$) upper limit in Table [2](#Input_data).

limitations_admitted.value: Proto-HC3N source sizes are lower limits because they are derived assuming optically thick v71 emission, making apparent luminosities lower limits prior to the greenhouse correction.

evidence.quote: We estimated a lower limit to the proto-HC$_3$N size from the line intensities of the rotational transition from the $v_{\rm 71}$ by assuming that their emission is optically thick.
These apparent luminosities of the proto-SSCs are, in principle, lower limits to the actual luminosity since we have used a lower limit to their sizes.

referee_caveats_inferred: The greenhouse correction factor (4/psi ~ 1/10) is adopted as a single representative value rather than modeled per source, introducing systematic uncertainty in L_p* and t_age.

Angular resolution differs by a factor of ~3 between ~100 GHz (0.14'' x 0.11'') and ~350 GHz (0.42'' x 0.37''), which can affect multi-transition LTE excitation fits if beam dilution and source structure are not matched.

Noticeable arithmetic/typographical inconsistency in Table 3 for proto-HC3N-6: L_p* ~ 0.84 and L_ZAMS = 0.20 would give L_p*/L_ZAMS = 4.2 rather than the printed ~0.42 (likely L_p* is 0.084 x 10^8 L_sun given T_vib=197 K and Size>0.36 pc).

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB (archival multi-band high-resolution spectral line cubes from two ALMA projects)
reproducibility.score_reason: Archival ALMA project codes, target coordinates, software tools (CASA 4.2.2, MADCUBA SLIM), and equations for physical quantities are clearly stated, but imaging details (continuum subtraction, clean thresholds) and intermediate LTE fit parameters (column densities, linewidths, exact extraction apertures) are omitted.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All raw data are public in the ALMA archive, the 14 SSC positions are tabulated, and the main results (T_rot, T_vib, sizes, luminosities, ages) are numeric and derived via a well-defined LTE + analytical pipeline.

methods_papers.why: Defines the methodology for deriving T_vib, T_rot, proto-SSC source sizes, greenhouse luminosity correction (4/psi ~ 1/10), and proto-SSC evolutionary ages from HC3N* LTE analysis.
Reference for the MADCUBA SLIM tool used for line identification and LTE modeling.
Provides the theoretical formulation for the greenhouse (back-warming) correction to apparent protostellar luminosity.

companion_papers.why: Provides the parent sample of 27 SSC candidates in NGC 4945, 90 GHz radio continuum ZAMS luminosities/masses, and gas masses.
Provides the ALMA CO molecular outflow maps and dynamical timescales in NGC 4945 used to establish positive feedback.
